statements.t: • risks associated with the expansion of our operations and properties, including through acquisitions and other strategic transactions, which may not be completed on anticipated terms, or at all;

• risks that we may be unable to deploy the turbine equipment acquired under the APA as planned, including because the Midcontinent Independent System Operator (“MISO”) does not approve our Expedited Resource Addition Study (“ERAS”) application or the related expansion project does not otherwise proceed, which could require us to sell the project together with the equipment or sell the equipment on a standalone…

• risks relating to our ability to participate in the MISO ERAS program, which ultimately requires the approval of MISO of our application and is a capital intensive project subject to construction, operational, financial, regulatory and legal risks that could impact the project’s viability and/or timeline;
• risks relating to our ability to secure agreements in support of the development and construction of planned projects, including the expansion of the Merom Station through the ERAS program;

• liquidity constraints, including due to restrictions contained in our debt agreements or other arrangements, limitations on our access to cash held in restricted and project-level accounts, and those resulting from any future unavailability of financing;

We continue to progress the development of the Turtle Creek Project, while monitoring opportunities to expand the capacity of our electric generation capabilities through further development, or via acquisition.
In addition, we focus our organic capital investments on strategic maintenance projects to maintain our safe operational performance and improve the reliability of Merom.
We expect to incur approximately $100.0 million of additional costs for transportation, refurbishment, insurance, and logistics in connection with the delivery of the equipment.

We retain the flexibility to determine the path that best creates value for shareholders, including advancing the full project, selling the project together with the equipment, or selling the equipment on a standalone basis.

At June 30, 2026, we forecasted full-year pretax income, whereas at September 30, 2026, we forecast a full-year pretax loss, primarily due to financing costs related to the KLIM Facility, including the loss on extinguishment of the TCB Credit Facility and interest expense, and expected operating results.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we estimated our annual ETR based upon projected annual income (loss), forecasted permanent tax differences, discrete items, and statutory rates in states in which we operate.

As of October 31, 2026, we had paid $349.8 million of the $350.0 million purchase price, with approximately $0.2 million remaining payable to third party vendors on behalf of the Seller, which will be paid in accordance with the APA.

We expect to fund these costs with cash on hand, cash from operations, and the delayed draw term loan commitment under the KLIM Facility, which is available only to fund the Turtle Creek Project, subject to funding conditions.
We expect our 2026 Capex to modestly increase as compared to our 2025 Capex, excluding any impacts of the Turtle Creek Project.

The actual amount of our 2026 Capex may vary from our expectations for a variety of reasons, including (i) changes in (a) the competitive o r regulatory environment, (b) business plans, or (c) our expected future operating results and (ii) the availability of sufficient capital.

Further, we anticipate that if we are able to enter into a Super Priority Revolver as permitted under the KLIM facility that there would be standard market terms and conditions related to the availability of funds.

statements.t: - Management Targets Approximately $1.6 Billion of Value from Turtle Creek Within 24 Months -

The Company is also providing an update on Turtle Creek Gas (“Turtle Creek”), its approximately 460-megawatt natural gas-fired generation project at the Merom site, which the Company is advancing toward a final investment decision (“FID”) targeted before the end of 2026.
“We believe the market ascribes little to no value to the project today.
The Company is targeting a final investment decision before year-end and is focused on securing long-term offtake agreements with investment-grade counterparties in early 2027.
As we advance toward our targeted commercial operation date in the second half of 2028, our objective is to build value at each development stage with little to no equity dilution.”
Our goal is FID before the end of 2026, and commencement of commercial operation remains targeted for the second half of 2028.”
Our estimates of the potential value of Turtle Creek reflect management’s current assumptions; they are not guidance or a prediction of our share price.
